scope: Internal standalone API pool key storage, waiter capacity and original pool credit lifetime. No aggregate HTTP/TLS connection bound, public API, package/platform or performance acceptance.

requirements.paragraph: Native standalone API request pools retain compact origin keys rather than backing allocations for complete request URLs. Reject authorities longer than 1040 bytes before pool lookup. Strict and ignored TLS verification keep separate clients but share one original 4 MiB context pool allowance. Retain that allowance through outstanding pooled connections, connection attempts and idle timer teardown; context disposal cannot reset it. Compact canceled or delivered waiter queues when their historical capacity exceeds twice the remaining length, with a four-slot floor. These pool ownership requirements do not establish the separate aggregate HTTP/TLS connection bound or public API release support.

regressionCases: 16 KiB owned request URI releases while compact origin remains idle.
Pending pooled owner retains original pool credit after final client drop.
Strict and ignored TLS clients share one 4 MiB allowance without an owner cycle.
Authority boundary accepts1040 and rejects1041 bytes.
Cancelled and delivered queues compact1024 slots to at most4 for one remaining waiter.
limitations: The larger conservative pool reservation reduces simultaneous empty-context admission under the engine metadata limit; this is not a performance claim.
Fixed runtime metadata reconciliation, outgoing Trailer amplification and aggregate TLS/HTTP phase proof remain open.
Idle timer custody was reviewed using source drop scopes, not a separate negative-control test.
Release build retains an existing unused timer parameter warning in upstream HyperUtil HTTP1-only configuration.
Frozen TypeScript host comes from the prior API checkpoint and does not cover concurrent runner edits.
